subject: Using source() to load functions from url (Sweave - Rnw)

messages.author: 7371c8f98f478526
messages.subject: Using source() to load functions from url (Sweave - Rnw)
parts:
I'm trying to use a function that is available in an url. However, it seems that the function source() did not load and the pdf output did not properly work. The warning message is "could not find function corvif". However, if a read in R Console I was able to run the analysis. Is there any way for using functions in urls?

You can see below a reproducible example

#### Reproducible Example


\documentclass{article}

\usepackage[latin9]{inputenc}
\begin{document}

<<echo=FALSE>>=
options(width=60)
@

\title{Analyses from the paper X}

\author{Diogo B. Provete, Thiago Gonçalves-Souza, Michel V. Garey, Itamar A. Martins and Denise de C. Rossa-Feres}

\maketitle
This document is a supplementary material and describes all the statistical analyses we used in this paper. Please, use the Table S1.txt provided to run the code. Feel free to contact the corresponding author if you have questions or comments. 
\subsubsection*{}
\maketitle
\textbf{Loading external functions}

<<LOAD FUNCTION>>=

source("http://bit.ly/dbp_corvif")

@

<<DATA&ANALYSIS>>=

dataset <- data.frame(a1=rnorm(100), a2=rnorm(100, 10, 2), a3=rnorm(20, 5))
corvif(dataset)

@


THANK YOU IN ADVANCE

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Using source() to load functions from url (Sweave - Rnw)
parts:
I cannot reproduce it. Please include sessionInfo() or see FAQ 1:
http://bit.ly/knitr-faq Also note that URL's are not guaranteed to
work, e.g. you may lose your Internet connection for some reason. I do
not recommend you to access code via URL.

Regards,
Yihui
